verdict.rationale: cubic's PR reviews use more than the diff. They auto-detect repo context files such as README.md and AGENTS.md, learn team conventions from feedback and historical reviews, and can link related repositories to check shared APIs and schemas. However, nothing documents that review comments analyze call sites or related modules across the whole repository; the 'reads the rest of your codebase' claim belongs to the AI chat sidebar, not the review. missing for 10: documented repo-wide call-site/dependency analysis in PR reviews, explicit related-module awareness within the same repo, independent hands-on corroboration of codebase-aware review comments

support.subject: As a developer, review comments reflect the whole repository — call sites, related modules, existing conventions — not just the changed hunks

citations.quote: cubic automatically detects and uses context files in your repository, including `README.md`, `context.md`, `AGENTS.md`, `.cursorrules`, agent skills directories, and files in `.ai/` directories.
Link related repositories so reviews can check shared APIs, schemas, docs, or release work.
cubic learns your team's unwritten rules from two sources: direct feedback on its comments, and patterns extracted from your senior engineers' historical code reviews.
